exposure: Attendance at a specialized multidisciplinary antenatal clinic for women with class III obesity
cohort: Women with a singleton pregnancy and class III obesity (BMI >40 kg/m2) who delivered in one of two hospitals in NHS Lothian, Scotland, UK between 2008 and 2014
finding: Attendance at a specialized antenatal clinic for obesity was associated with reduced rates of stillbirth and low birth weight, and improved detection of gestational diabetes.
mod_finding: Women attending the specialized obesity clinic were more likely to require induction of labor (38.4% vs 29.9%) and both elective (20.3% vs 17.7%) and emergency (23.9% vs 20.3%) caesarean sections compared to those receiving standard care.
